title: Buffered I/O
concept: Buffered I/O improves performance by reducing the number of system calls, but requires understanding when to flush.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
**`#include <stdio.h>`** — Header for using standard input/output functions such as `printf` and `fflush`.

In this lesson you will learn **Buffering**.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
**`int main() {`** — When a program starts, the operating system opens standard streams and sets the **buffering mode** for each.

steps.title: store data in buffer
steps.explanation:
**`printf("Example 1... ");`** — You called `printf`, but there was no **`\n` at the end of the string**.

The current location of the data is the `stdout` internal buffer in memory.

steps.explanation:
**`printf("Printed immediately!
");`** — This `printf` contains **`

steps.title: Automatic flush recheck
steps.explanation: **`printf("Example 2 with newline\n");`** — Since `\n` is included, per-line buffering is automatically flushed and printed to the screen immediately.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation: **`return 0;`** — Upon normal termination, the C runtime automatically flushes the buffers of all open streams. Data that was `printf`ed without `\n` at the end is also output at this point.

quiz.question: When a program crashes and terminates, why may the printf contents not appear on the screen?
options: This is because the output buffer could not be emptied and the process died.
Because the printf function is slow
quiz.explanation:
If there is data in the buffer without a newline (\n) or fflush and a crash occurs, the data does not appear on the screen and disappears.
Be careful when debugging.

misconceptions.wrong: All input and output are processed immediately.
misconceptions.correct: Buffering is almost always involved to reduce disk I/O and system call costs (Full, Line, No buffering).
misconceptions.why: This is because system calls are expensive operations.

keyTakeaway: Buffering improves performance, but when you need real-time output or are debugging, you need to understand the importance of fflush.
